howParkingWorks:
All claims below were read from primary sources on 2026-10-01 unless marked UNVERIFIED. WebSearch/WebFetch were unavailable in this session, so discovery was by direct fetch of official sites only (no news check).

1) GENERAL RULE (changed in 2022/23, many older sources and the BA Data file are out of date). Código de Tránsito y Transporte (Ley 2148, Anexo I), art. 7.1.2, text as replaced by Ley 6546 (published 11/07/2022, art. 3 in force 180 days later) and as served in the "texto actualizado" dated 28/07/2025 at https://boletinoficial.buenosaires.gob.ar/normativaba/norma/95322 : (a) avenidas: parking prohibited on BOTH sides on business days ("días hábiles") 7:00 to 21:00; (b) calles: parking permitted on BOTH sides 24h; (c) streets/avenues with Metrobús: prohibited both sides 24h; (d) streets/avenues with a ciclovía: prohibited next to the ciclovía lane 24h. The old "one side only" rule for calles is gone. GCBA plain-language page confirms and adds that on avenues you may park 21:00 to 7:00 on business days and 24h on weekends and holidays; pasajes, Metrobús arteries, "calles de convivencia" and the space parallel to ciclovías are prohibited 24h: https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/jefaturadegabinete/movilidad/transporte/normas-de-estacionamiento (the /gcaba_historico/ path is the live legacy CMS, it carries Sept 2026 news).

2) PARTICULAR RULES PER BLOCK ("regímenes especiales", art. 7.1.16). Set by the authority by administrative act and they override the general rule; a vertical sign is mandatory only for these (art. 7.1.12), so the general rule is unsigned. Legal list: Resolución 216/SECTOP/23, Anexo I (IF-2023-14235761-GCABA-DGGSM, 63 pages, table ARTERIA / DESDE / HASTA / LADO / NORMA / HORARIO), in force since 17/04/2023, "texto actualizado" last updated 29/09/2026: https://boletinoficial.buenosaires.gob.ar/normativaba/norma/655911 . Only two schedules exist in law and data: "24 HORAS" and "DIAS HABILES DE 7 A 21 HORAS". Norm types: PERMITIDO ESTACIONAR, PROHIBIDO ESTACIONAR, PROHIBIDO ESTACIONAR Y DETENERSE, PERMITIDO A 45°, A 90°, PARALELO A CICLOVIA.

3) BLANKET PROHIBITIONS INSIDE A BLOCK (arts. 7.1.8 and 7.1.9, apply even where the block is "permitted"): double parking, corners/ochavas, crosswalks, tunnels/bridges, on ciclovías; pasajes with roadway up to 4.5 m and calles de convivencia; within 50 m of level crossings; bus and taxi stops (GCBA page: if unpainted, 15 m before and 10 m after the stop); garage entrances; in front of venues during shows, police stations, fire stations, ramps (vados), subway entrances, funeral homes 8 to 22; within 10 m of entrances of hospitals/clinics, schools in class hours, temples during services, hotels with 30+ rooms, banks and post offices in opening hours; reserved spaces; next to exclusive lanes during their operating hours; feria barrial sectors on market days; signed loading zones. Heavy vehicles (buses, trucks, trailers, motorhomes) may not park on street at all (7.1.4). Curb colors (art. 2.4.4.1 as per Ley 6546): yellow = no parking 24h, orange = exclusive for bikes/motorcycles.

4) METERED PARKING ("Sistema de Estacionamiento Regulado", Code chapter 7.4). Official page: https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/estacionamiento-medido . Since June 2022 there are no meters or tokens; payment is by the Blinkay app (iOS/Android), web https://caba.blinkay.app/ , or cash at participating shops. Hours (Code 7.4.7 and page): business days 8:00 to 20:00, Saturdays 8:00 to 13:00, Sundays and holidays free. Zone: parts of San Telmo, Monserrat, Balvanera, San Nicolás, Retiro, Recoleta, Puerto Madero and Almagro; boundary per GCBA: Av. Ing. Huergo, Av. San Juan, Av. Paseo Colón, Av. Independencia, Perú, Venezuela, Bernardo de Irigoyen, Av. Belgrano, Av. Jujuy, Av. Pueyrredón, Av. Córdoba, Agüero, Peña, Av. Pueyrredón, Av. Figueroa Alcorta, C. Della Paolera, Av. Eduardo Madero, plus the Hospital Italiano surroundings (Corrientes, Salguero, Díaz Vélez, Río de Janeiro, Lambaré). Two tariff modes per block: Simple and Progresiva. Page states: first hour $1000; each next hour's increment is +30% over the previous (cumulative $2300, $3990, $6187 at 4 h), then $2197 per extra hour; minimum 15 min, 5 min steps, max 12 h; prepago or postpago. The peso values are as printed on the page today; whether they are still current is UNVERIFIED. Enforcement: Agentes de Tránsito with plate-reading cameras on vehicles (official FAQ https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/noticias/preguntas-frecuentes ). New sectors need legislative approval (7.4.1, 7.4.11). Any expansion beyond this zone in 2025/2026 is UNVERIFIED (not found in the norms linked to the Code).

5) RESIDENTS. Residents of the tariffed zone park free within a 300 m radius of home (Code 7.4.5; page https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/infraestructura/movilidad/beneficio-para-residentes ): one vehicle per person and per dwelling, ABL number required, valid 2 years, no reserved space, checked by plate. The Code (7.4.6) allows reserving 20% to 40% of spaces for residents; whether any are actually reserved is UNVERIFIED. There is no resident permit outside the tariffed zone.

6) LOADING ZONES. "Cajones azules": exclusive loading/unloading boxes, max 30 minutes unless the sign says otherwise, hazard lights on, days and hours on the sign (Code 7.1.10; https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/infraestructura/movilidad/espacio-de-carga-y-descarga ).

7) TOWING ("acarreo", Code art. 2.1.5). Tow is allowed for violations of 7.1.2 (general rule, so the weekday avenue ban is towable), 7.1.3, 7.1.6, 7.1.8 and most of 7.1.9; only a public official or traffic agent can order it even if a concessionaire operates the trucks. Free tows: feria sectors, crashes, force majeure, tree pruning/public works. Unpaid meter time (7.4.13) is not in the tow list. Impound lots, open 24h all year (https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/acarreo ): Av. 9 de Julio y Sarmiento (underground) for Viamonte to Av. Belgrano; Tacuarí 1277 south of Av. Belgrano; Eduardo J. Couture (behind Facultad de Derecho) north of Viamonte; Ramón Falcón 4785 (Villa Luro) for the western zone. A sticker is left where the car was. Tow fee and which companies operate today: UNVERIFIED.

8) FINES (Régimen de Faltas, Ley 451, text served at https://boletinoficial.buenosaires.gob.ar/normativaba/norma/8540 ; version date not confirmed). 6.1.52 prohibited parking/stopping: 100 Unidades Fijas; doubled in emergency reserves, bus stops, vehicle entrances, ciclovías, exclusive lanes, Metrobús corridors and Microcentro/Macrocentro; 300 UF in disability spaces or ramps. 6.1.53 metered overstay up to one hour beyond paid time: 100 UF. 6.1.54 pedestrian areas or sidewalks: 300 UF. One UF = half a litre of premium petrol, fixed each semester (art. 20). Current UF value in pesos: UNVERIFIED.

9) STREET CLEANING. There is no sweeping-based parking prohibition anywhere in Título 7 or in the tow causes of art. 2.1.5 (both read in full), and BA Data (454 datasets) has no barrido schedule. Sweeping is not a parking event in CABA. Temporary signed operations are possible but UNVERIFIED.

10) OTHER. Disability emblem gives free parking except in 7.1.8/7.1.9 places (7.1.18) and those cars cannot be towed while using it (7.1.19). Motorcycles follow car rules and must use marked moto sectors where they exist (7.1.21). Authority of application: Ministerio de Infraestructura (Decreto 282/25); the curb data owner is "GO Estacionamiento Ordenado y Regulación del Cordón, DG Gestión Integral del Tránsito, Secretaría de Tránsito". Official "can I park here" channels today: WhatsApp bot Boti 11-5050-0147 (word "Estacionamiento") and the IDECABA viewer layer "Estacionamiento en vía pública - Normativa".

datasets.need: Curb rules per block side with geometry (the core layer, equivalent to SF sweeping segments)
datasets.name: IDECABA GeoServer: catalogo_og_130:estacionamiento_normativa ("Estacionamiento en vía pública - Normativa")
datasets.api: OGC WFS/WMS: https://geoserver.buenosaires.gob.ar/geoserver/catalogo_og_130/ows?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetFeature&typeNames=catalogo_og_130:estacionamiento_normativa&outputFormat=application/json&srsName=EPSG:4326 (also csv, kml, gml; bbox= supported). CORS: access-control-allow-origin: * on GET, HEAD and OPTIONS preflight, works without a browser User-Agent. Full download 26 MB took 127 s; a 1 km bbox returned 307 features in 2.7 s. No cached vector tiles (gwc pbf returned 400); WMS GetMap PNG works with CORS *.
datasets.fields: id, fna, gna, nam (street), tvc (Calle/Avenida/Pasaje/Sendero/Boulevard/Calle Peatonal), ldo (derecho/izquierdo), ade, aha (address from/to), rgl (rule+schedule in one string), trf (tariff type or null), sag. Sample: {id:28528, nam:"GORRITI", tvc:"Calle", ldo:"derecho", ade:4301, aha:4400, rgl:"PERMITIDO ESTACIONAR 24 HORAS", trf:null, sag:"Secretaría de Tránsito"}. rgl has exactly 7 values: PERMITIDO ESTACIONAR 24 HORAS (34,949), PROHIBIDO ESTACIONAR 24 HORAS (8,771), PROHIBIDO ESTACIONAR DIAS HABILES DE 7 A 21 HORAS (5,339), PROHIBIDO ESTACIONAR Y DETENERSE 24 HORAS (2,297), PERMITIDO A 45° (204), A 90° (103), PARALELO A CICLOVIA (92). trf values: PROGRESIVA, SIMPLE, plus variants with LOGISTICA and MOTOS (2,734 features non-null).
datasets.geometry: MultiLineString, one line per SIDE of each block, already offset from the centerline (two parallel lines about 10 m apart per block). 51,755 features, about 4,634 km of curb (my planar estimate): 66% permitted 24h, 17.5% prohibited 24h, 10.8% prohibited business days 7 to 21, 4.8% no stopping. Native CRS EPSG:9498, served in 4326 on request. Join key to centerlines: nam + ade/aha.
datasets.freshness: Metadata date 2026-03-01 (record stamped 2026-03-09). Update cadence not stated. The legal source (Res. 216/23 annex) was last updated 2026-09-29, so the layer may lag by months.
datasets.license: GeoNetwork record: use must cite the source; "queda estrictamente prohibido cualquier aprovechamiento o explotación ... con fines comerciales"; informative/educational use allowed with attribution. This is stricter than BA Data's CC-BY 2.5 AR. Needs written confirmation for CURB.
datasets.notes: Verified empirically against the callejero (44,916 matched segments, 98% consistent) that ldo is relative to the DIRECTION OF TRAFFIC (as the metadata says); on two-way streets derecho = right of increasing numbering = odd side. 606 features have ade=0 (unnumbered). trf is set on both sides of tariffed blocks including sides where parking is prohibited 24h (986 cases), so trf means "block is in the tariffed system", not "this side is payable"; and 149 of the 737 block sides in the official Feb 2025 PDF have no trf here. Treat trf as a hint only. Local copies: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-alevizio/a6671fb0-a56b-4a27-8d89-29245b7ea378/scratchpad/ba/norm.geojson and norm.csv

productFit:
WHAT IT SHOULD SHOW. Not sweeping. The Buenos Aires question is "can I leave the car on this side of this block right now, until when, and do I have to pay". The whole city reduces to a small state machine per curb side, which is simpler than SF:
- Free 24h (66% of curb km).
- Never (prohibited 24h, or no stopping) (22%).
- Time-limited: prohibited business days 7:00 to 21:00, mostly avenues (11%, about 500 km, 5,339 block sides). This is the Buenos Aires equivalent of the sweeping window: a recurring, predictable, towable restriction that starts at 7:00 on the next business day. It is also unsigned on most avenues because it is the general rule.
- Metered overlay: Mon to Fri business days 8:00 to 20:00, Sat 8:00 to 13:00, with Simple or Progresiva tariff, pay in Blinkay.
Map coloring: each side colored by current state plus time to next change (green free, red no, amber "ok until 7:00 Mon", blue metered now). Block sheet: rule text as published, schedule, tariff mode and hours, link to Blinkay, fine in UF and tow risk, the standing in-block prohibitions as a checklist (garage entrances, bus stops, ramps, 10 m from schools/hospitals/banks in hours), nearest impound lot. Alerts: "you parked on an avenue side, move before 7:00 on the next business day" (holiday-aware), "metering starts at 8:00", "paid time ends". Layers: metered blocks, loading zones, Metrobús/ciclovías, garages, ferias by weekday.

FEASIBLE NOW FROM OPEN DATA.
- Full citywide curb map from one layer: catalogo_og_130:estacionamiento_normativa (51,755 pre-offset side lines, 7 rule values, 2 schedules). CORS is open, but a full pull is 26 MB and takes about 2 minutes, so bake it into tiles at build time and refresh on a schedule; do not fetch it from the client.
- Side semantics are solved: ldo is relative to traffic direction, and joining to the callejero (sentido + odd/even ranges) gives odd/even side and avenue/calle type. Verified on 44,916 segments.
- Address search and "where am I" from USIG normalizar and reversegeocoding (CORS *, no key); the reverse geocoder returns the block range string that keys into the curb layer.
- Time engine: only two schedule strings plus the metered hours, plus a holiday table.
- Metered overlay from the Feb 2025 PDF (737 block sides), joined by street + range + side.
- Context layers: Metrobús, ciclovías, bus stops, taxi stands, ramps, schools, ferias with weekday and hours, garages (old).
- A "complaint heat" layer from SUACI "Vehículo mal estacionado" reports as an enforcement proxy.

NOT FEASIBLE OR WEAK.
- Sub-block precision. Sign-level rules, garage entrances, bus stop lengths, reserved spaces (disability, embassies, works), loading zone hours, decks, and yellow or orange curbs are not in any dataset. The app can say "this side allows parking" but not "this exact spot is legal". Must be stated in the UI.
- Exact metered status per side: trf in the layer is inconsistent with the official PDF, and the PDF is from Feb 2025.
- Ticket or tow risk by block and hour: no citation or tow data is published.
- Current prices in pesos (tariff and fines) change often; fetch or hand-maintain, do not hardcode.
- Real-time: closures, events, temporary prohibitions. API Transporte is gated and marked suspended.
- Resident free-parking radius is per address and resolved inside the government system; can only be approximated as a 300 m circle.

RISKS. (1) License: the IDECABA record forbids commercial exploitation; BA Data's CC-BY copy is the 2020 file with the old rule. Get written permission or a CC-BY republication before launch. (2) Freshness: layer dated March 2026 while the legal annex changed in Sept 2026. Show the data date. (3) There is an official answer channel already (Boti on WhatsApp and the IDECABA viewer), so the value is the map, time awareness and alerts, not the raw rule.

MULTI-CITY IMPLICATION. The city adapter needs: curb-side segments with a rule enum and schedule set, a side convention (traffic-relative vs numbering-relative), a business-day calendar, an optional metered overlay with its own hours, and a "primary recurring restriction" concept that is sweeping in SF and the weekday avenue ban in Buenos Aires. Working files from this research are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-alevizio/a6671fb0-a56b-4a27-8d89-29245b7ea378/scratchpad/ba/ (norm.geojson, norm.csv, d_callejero.csv, tramos.txt, codigo.txt, l451.txt, all.json); it is a session scratch directory, copy anything worth keeping.
gaps: No traffic sign inventory (vertical signs) is published; BA Data and the GeoServer have none. Sign-level hours and partial-block rules are invisible.
No citation or infraction data with time and location, and no tow (acarreo) records or tow-zone polygons. Only a per-plate lookup form exists. SUACI complaints are the only proxy.

Metered blocks: the only authoritative list is a PDF from Feb 2025; the trf field in the March 2026 layer disagrees with it (149 PDF block sides have no trf; 986 sides with trf are prohibited 24h; extra streets such as Mitre, Corrientes, Pueyrredón carry trf). Meaning of the LOGISTICA and MOTOS tariff variants is undocumented. No zone polygon is published.
Current tariff in pesos is UNVERIFIED as current (page shows $1000 first hour with +30% progressive steps); current Unidad Fija value in pesos and the tow fee are UNVERIFIED.
Any 2025/2026 expansion of metered parking to new neighbourhoods is UNVERIFIED: web search was unavailable in this session, and nothing appeared among the norms linked to the Code.
License conflict: the current curb layer (IDECABA) carries a non-commercial clause; the CC-BY 2.5 AR copy on BA Data is from Q1 2020 and encodes the pre-2022 one-side rule.
Update cadence of estacionamiento_normativa is not stated (metadata date 2026-03-01; legal annex updated 2026-09-29). No changelog or versioning.
Loading zones (2019, points, no hours), garages (2019, from a 2016 survey, no prices or hours), motorcycle boxes (2019, 42 rows) are stale.

No data for garage entrances/driveways, bus stop extents, reserved spaces (disability, diplomatic, works), restaurant decks currently installed, yellow/orange curb paint, or ordinary bus-only lanes with their operating hours.
Ciclovías data does not say which side of the street the lane occupies; bus stops are points without side.
No official machine-readable holiday feed; unclear whether bridge days and "días no laborables" count as non-business days for art. 7.1.2 and for metering.
606 curb features have no address range (ade = 0), and about 2% of side labels did not match the traffic-direction test.
Whether resident-reserved spaces (Code 7.4.6) exist on street is UNVERIFIED.
Street cleaning: no schedule data and no rule tying it to parking; temporary signed clean-up operations are UNVERIFIED.

Operational fragility: data.buenosaires.gob.ar sits behind a WAF that rejects non-browser user agents and challenges bursts; cdn.buenosaires.gob.ar has no CORS; full WFS pulls are slow. API Transporte is gated and flagged as suspended.
The Ley 451 text I read came from the Boletín Oficial normativa portal without a visible version date; fine amounts should be rechecked against the current consolidated text.

Research limits: WebSearch and WebFetch hit a session limit and the Chrome extension was not connected, so everything came from direct curl fetches of official hosts. Pages on buenosaires.gob.ar/tramites/... about vehicle retention returned "no permission".
